channel.title: Cursor Research
channel.description: Research articles from Cursor's official Research topic.

item.title: Improved token efficiency for longer agent runs
item.description: Changes across Cursor's agent harness reduced token costs for users by 7% without reducing agent quality.

item.title: Introducing Grok 4.6
item.description: Built for long-running agents and more ambitious interactive and visual work.

item.title: How Cursor Router chooses the right model for the task
item.description: Auto Intelligence now delivers above Fable-level satisfaction at 68% lower cost. Here's how Compass and the task router choose models from real developer traffic.

item.title: Mixture-of-Kittens: our open-source MoE megakernel for NVL72s
item.description: We're open-sourcing Mixture-of-Kittens, a deterministic MoE training megakernel for NVL72s that fuses communication and computation into a single kernel.

item.title: How we set up our cloud agent environment
item.description: Getting our monorepo working for cloud agents taught us that the development environment is a product in its own right, only one whose users are agents.

item.title: Agent swarms and the new model economics
item.description: We compared old and new agent swarms building SQLite from scratch and found that better coordination delivers similar quality at a fraction of the cost.

item.title: Grok 4.5 Model Card
item.description: The official model card for Grok 4.5. It documents the model's capability benchmarks and safety evaluations.

item.title: Introducing Grok 4.5
item.description: Our most intelligent model and the first we've built for more than software engineering.

item.title: Reward hacking is swamping model intelligence gains
item.description: On SWE-bench Pro, 63% of successful Opus 4.8 Max resolutions retrieved the fix rather than derived it. Stricter eval harnesses show how benchmark scores can conflate coding ability with answer retrieval.

item.title: Governing agent autonomy with Auto-review
item.description: Auto-review uses a classifier agent to govern local agent autonomy, allowing low-stakes actions to run freely while slowing down when an action crosses a meaningful boundary.
